question: P is any point inside the rectangle ABCD. If PA = 86 cm, PB = 49 cm and PC = 79 cm, then the length of PD (in cm) is equal to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By British Flag Theorem: PA² + PC² = PB² + PD²

⇒ 86² + 79² = 49² + PD²

⇒ 7396 + 6241 = 2401 + PD²

⇒ 13637 − 2401 = PD²

⇒ PD = √11236 = 106 cm

**∴ The correct option is A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Rectangle ABCD with internal point P.

PA = 86 cm, PB = 49 cm, PC = 79 cm.

**Formula Used:**

British Flag Theorem: For any point P inside or outside a rectangle ABCD, the sum of the squares of the distances from P to opposite vertices is equal.

PA² + PC² = PB² + PD²

 
• 
• 
• 
• A B C D P 86 cm 49 cm 79 cm PD = ? 

**Calculations:**

⇒ PA² + PC² = PB² + PD²

⇒ 86² + 79² = 49² + PD²

⇒ 7396 + 6241 = 2401 + PD²

⇒ 13637 = 2401 + PD²

⇒ PD² = 13637 − 2401

⇒ PD² = 11236

⇒ PD = √11236

⇒ PD = 106 cm

**∴ The correct option is A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

British Flag Theorem

This theorem states that for any point P and rectangle ABCD, PA² + PC² = PB² + PD². It holds true even if P is outside the rectangle or on its boundary.

Rectangle Diagonals

The diagonals of a rectangle are equal in length and bisect each other. Diagonal length d = √(l² + w²).

Pythagoras Theorem in Rectangles

Any diagonal divides the rectangle into two congruent right-angled triangles where the diagonal acts as the hypotenuse.
